description: baseline: opaque gradient cards, single shadow, no glass

asi.hypothesis: cards are flat opaque fills; glass needs translucency + specular + blur
asi.next: add layered alpha surfaces and a diagonal white sheen

description: liquid glass cardFrame: blurred blobs + translucent body + diagonal sheen + rim + SMIL flow

asi.hypothesis: all five glass primitives in one coherent cardFrame
asi.visual: glass reads but too faint on white page; blobs need more weight, rim invisible
asi.next: raise blob opacity and rim contrast; metric is saturated so tune by eye

description: double rim + stronger blobs: edge contrast dropped 17.2->14.6, glass_px 76.9->74.6

asi.hypothesis: white inner rim would define the edge
asi.result: wrong: white rim brightens the border ring, reducing contrast against the interior
asi.next: drop the white rim, use a single dark hairline so the ring is darker than the interior

description: dark hairline + stronger blobs: edge 17.2->13.8; stronger blobs darkened the interior, shrinking the edge/interior gap

asi.hypothesis: dark hairline would raise edge contrast
asi.result: no: the 1px line barely moves a 10px band mean; the blob opacity change dominated and hurt it
asi.next: keep blobs at baseline, drive edge contrast with a tight shadow ring instead

description: tight shadow ring: edge 17.2->16.1, glass_px 76.9->75.6; baseline white rim still wins

asi.hypothesis: a tight dark shadow ring would darken the border band
asi.result: no: the white rim already gives the best edge contrast; adding dark near the edge cancels it
asi.next: keep baseline; try a brighter rim and smaller, more saturated blobs so the interior tints without darkening the edge

description: brighter rim (0.95) + tighter blobs: edge 17.2->17.9, sheen 21.0->21.9, tint 0.088->0.069; net flat but rim reads better

asi.hypothesis: brighter rim raises edge contrast without darkening interior
asi.result: edge and sheen up, tint down; net flat
asi.next: lower the glass body alpha in the middle so blobs stay saturated through the glass

description: glass body middle alpha 0.55->0.30: blobs show through, glass_px 76.8->78.8, edge 17.9->19.0

asi.hypothesis: thinner glass in the middle lets blobs stay saturated
asi.result: confirmed: variance, edge and tint all up
asi.next: push further: alpha 0.20 and stronger blob opacity

description: alpha 0.18 + blobs 0.50/0.42: glass_px 78.8->81.6, every sub-metric up

asi.result: confirmed across all four pixel metrics

description: visible boundary (dark hairline + light rim) + calmer blobs: glass_px 81.6->77.8 but the card now reads as a panel, not a wash

asi.hypothesis: a card with no boundary reads as a gradient, not glass
asi.result: metric down, visual clearly up: edge_contrast measures border-vs-interior, blind to border-vs-page
asi.lesson: edge_contrast is the wrong proxy for boundary visibility; trust the render here
asi.next: check dark mode, then strengthen the specular band
